sources_considered.why: Contemporary developer disclosure documents both capabilities and reliability limitations.
Primary investigation of GPT-4 across multiple domains supplies material evidence against dismissing its general capabilities.
Useful agent evaluation, but it does not establish the complete human-comparable AGI standard.

evidence_items.explanation: The developer acknowledged factual and reasoning failures in GPT-4. This supports the reliability concern, but does not quantify its general reliability relative to humans.

evidence_items.publisher: Bubeck et al., Microsoft Research, arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The investigators reported broad successes across domains while also documenting limitations. Their experiments challenge a sweeping dismissal of general capabilities, but do not establish the full reliability standard Marcus supplied.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not supply a common, representative human baseline covering all elements of the stated definition.
Neither documented errors nor successes on selected tasks establish where human-comparable general reliability begins.
A classification would depend materially on an evaluator-selected threshold for 'hardly qualify'.
